_readme: THE PROVIDER REGISTER — [pipeline K-5] Private/requirements/ (was pipeline/08-compliance-legal.md, folded into the JSON spec 2026-08-15)
Every third party that touches a payment, a user's data, or the delivery of the Services: what role
it plays, whether the published pages name it, and — the field the whole file hangs off — whether it
is REACHABLE IN CODE today.
WHY IT EXISTS. K-5 says 'the commercial surface names the actual seller and payment path'. Nothing
compared the two. At the moment this register landed the three published pages and the code disagreed
in four independent places, and no build anywhere could go red over any of them:
· services/subscriptiontracker-api/src/routes/webhooks.ts declares POST /revenuecat. RevenueCat is named in no
published page and in no ADR. ⏱ 2026-09-16: that route is RETIRED; RevenueCat is reached through
services/platform's POST /v1/money/:provider (its revenuecatVerifier), and privacy.html names it.
· [ADR 004] LOCKED Paddle as the merchant of record on 2026-07-23. Paddle is named in none of
privacy.html, terms.html or refund.html. ✅ HALF FIXED — terms.html §4 and refund.html §2/§4 now
name Paddle and describe the merchant-of-record role ([ADR 039]). privacy.html still says only
'a merchant of record' and is the remaining half, because that page is inside the policy-VERSION
surface: correcting it is a version bump plus an archive snapshot (assert-policy-archive.mjs),
which is one owner signature covering every privacy.html correction at once, not three.
· terms.html and refund.html say website purchases are processed by Razorpay, while privacy.html
says 'We do not sell anything directly from this website today'. The pages contradict each other.
✅ FIXED — the `website-seller-contradiction` gap was retired when the wording landed. All three
pages now agree that nothing is sold directly from the website yet; the two that are not version-
gated additionally name the seller that will take the payment.
· privacy.html says usage statistics AND CRASH REPORTS run on infrastructure provided by
Cloudflare. Crash reports run on Oracle Cloud (Private/runbooks/glitchtip.md). ✅ FIXED at the
2026-08-10 signature, which split the sentence so each system names its own host. ⏱ AND THE HOST
ITSELF THEN MOVED: GlitchTip left Box A for Box B on 2026-09-02, so from that date the split
sentence named the right SHAPE and the wrong MACHINE. Corrected in the 2026-09-05 mint — the sink
row is now `hostinger` and the page names Hostinger. See that row's notes.
🔴 EVERY ONE OF THOSE IS FIXED BY EDITING A PUBLISHED LEGAL PAGE, WHICH IS OWNER WORK (OWNER_QUEUE
O-3). They are therefore carried as `disclosureGap` rows that PRINT on every run — never silently
exempted, and never made a build failure, because failing CI on copy only the owner can write blocks
every other lane on this repository. tooling/ci/assert-policy-claims.mjs FAILS the moment a gap row's
stated reason stops being true, so an exemption cannot outlive what it was granted for.
⚠️ WHAT IS PUBLIC HERE AND WHAT IS NOT. This is a public repository. A row records the provider's
NAME, its ROLE, where the code reaches it and whether a page discloses it. It records nothing about
the merchant account itself — no merchant ids, no KYC state, no bank or payout details, no contract
terms. Those live in the private SSoT and a row points at them by NAME only, in `privateRecord`,
the same split tooling/channel-register.json uses for signing custody. See tooling/legal/README.md.
Enforced by tooling/ci/assert-policy-claims.mjs:
· every claims row typed `provider` resolves to a row here                        [K-5]
· every row with `reachableAt` names a route path that really exists in services/  [K-5]
· every route path segment in services/** is either a provider row's tell or is
named in `nonProviderRouteSegments` below — so a NEW payment webhook cannot be
added without somebody writing its name down                                     [K-5]
· a `merchant_of_record` row with status `live` MUST be named in BOTH terms.html
and refund.html; one that is not yet live PRINTS with its owner item             [K-5]
· every row's `status` is in `statuses` below; a `silent` status (deferred, retired,
not-named-not-wired) never prints a missing disclosure                           [K-5]
· every `disclosureGap` row carries an ownerItem and a `stillTrue` probe, and the
guard FAILS when the probe stops matching — the gap is resolved, retire the row   [C-6 split]
· COVERAGE LOST on an empty register or zero route paths extracted                 [F-10]
And by tooling/ci/assert-sink-disclosure.mjs — THE SINK-DISCLOSURE LIMB:
· every `infrastructure` row with status `live` DECLARES the personal-data
categories it receives and retains (`receives`), with a stated `receivesBasis`   [K-5]
· every published "we do not collect / do not store X" denial is SCOPED against
the union of those declarations, and FAILS when a live sink declares what a
page denies                                                                      [K-5]
· a denial that resolves to NO declared category FAILS unless it is classified
in `denialsOutOfScope` — a new denial cannot be published unscoped               [K-5]
· COVERAGE LOST on zero live infrastructure rows, an empty declared union, or
zero denials extracted from the pages                                            [F-10]
`requiredWhen` — ON EVERY ROW. The condition under which an app must declare this provider in its
apps/<id>/privacy.yaml `processors`, evaluated by tooling/legal/required-providers.mjs against the
app's own app.yaml and the laned app channels of tooling/channel-register.json (surface app, lane not null).
One of five kinds:
· always          every app with a privacy declaration: the shared stack
· appYaml         {path, equals}: the app's app.yaml carries that dotted key with that value
· mobileIapRail   {rail}: the app declares billing.mobileIap AND a laned app channel sells on that rail
· channelRail     {rail, regionToo?}: a laned app channel sells on that rail (with regionToo, or names
it in purchaseRail.regionRails)
· never           {why}: no app configuration makes it a processor; `why` is at least 20 characters
A key starting with `_` is a comment. Enforced by tooling/ci/assert-app-yaml.mjs limb 9: a required
provider missing from a privacy.yaml, or a `never` provider declared in one, is a finding (exit 1); a
row with no requiredWhen, or a kind the resolver does not know, is COVERAGE LOST (exit 2).
O-APP-PRIVACY-OMITS-STORE-BILLING.

_why: 🔴 THIS IS THE HALF THAT MAKES THE ROUTE LIMB UNFAKEABLE, and it is data rather than a list
inside the guard on purpose. The guard extracts every literal path segment registered in
services/**/src/**/*.ts. A segment is allowed to exist only if it is either a provider row's
tell (RevenueCat's `/revenuecat`) or is written down HERE as a resource of ours.
So adding `app.post('/paddle', …)` — or `/stripe`, or `/lemonsqueezy` — turns the build RED
until somebody either adds the provider row or claims the segment as ours. There is no third
option and no way to pad the allowlist except by naming the thing you are adding.
⚠️ `:param` segments are dropped before the comparison, not listed here: `/:id` and `/:app` are
placeholders, and listing them would be listing the syntax rather than a resource.
_box-manifest: 🟢 `ops` and `box-manifest` ADDED 2026-10-03 (PB-27), AND THIS LIMB CAUGHT THEM. POST
/v1/ops/box-manifest on services/platform is our own box cron
(tooling/ops/boxes/post-config-manifest.sh) reporting config HASHES. It is a RESOURCE OF OURS
and not a provider tell: the bearer is checked against that one box's own secret
(BOX_SECRET_ENV in services/platform/src/routes/box-manifest.ts), no provider posts to it, it
moves no money, and a request carrying `Origin` is refused on `/v1/ops/`
(services/platform/src/middleware/cors.ts). If anything external ever posts here, this entry
becomes false and a provider row is owed instead.
_payments: 🟢 `payments` ADDED 2026-09-29 (ST-R5, round-2 X06), AND THIS LIMB CAUGHT IT. POST
/v1/subscriptions/:id/payments on services/subscriptiontracker-api is the user marking one of
THEIR OWN tracked subscriptions as paid: a payment_history row with `source` = manual, a record
OF a payment the user made elsewhere. It is a RESOURCE OF OURS and not a provider tell: no
provider posts to it, it moves no money, it is behind supabaseAuth, and the body is an amount and
a date the user typed. The name is the one this limb exists to question, which is why it is
written down here rather than inferred.
_subject: 🟢 `subject` ADDED 2026-09-09, AND THIS LIMB CAUGHT IT AGAIN. GET /v1/entitlements/subject is the
"what do I own" read the per-app route cannot answer — [ADR 057] §5, the bundle union. It is a
RESOURCE OF OURS and not a provider tell: nothing posts to it, it takes no body, and it is behind
platformAuth like the route it sits under.
⚠️ IT IS LISTED BECAUSE THE GUARD IS RIGHT TO ASK. A new segment under a Worker that already
carries the money rail is exactly where a payment webhook would land unnoticed, and the answer
has to be written down by the person adding it rather than inferred from the name.
_receipts: 🟢 `receipts` ADDED 2026-09-09, AND THIS LIMB CAUGHT IT AGAIN. POST /v1/receipts/:store is a
RESOURCE OF OURS and NOT a provider tell, and the distinction is the whole design: a provider
tell is a segment the PROVIDER posts to (RevenueCat's `/revenuecat`), whereas nothing external
posts here at all. Our own authenticated client posts an opaque store token, and the SERVER then
calls the store's API itself — the push is never the evidence ([ADR 057]; the bundle entitlement
design §3.2). Google's RTDN carries no proof in its body and Microsoft has no push whatsoever.
⚠️ THIS IS EXACTLY THE SEGMENT THE LIMB EXISTS FOR. A route named `receipts` under the Worker that
already carries the money rail is where a payment webhook would land unnoticed, and the answer has
to be written down by the person adding it rather than inferred from the name. If a store rail
ever DOES push here, this entry becomes false and a provider row is owed instead.
_checkout: 🟢 `checkout` ADDED 2026-08-12, AND THIS LIMB CAUGHT IT AGAIN — the third time. The route
create-transaction server half, [ADR 044]) and it passed typecheck, its own tests and every
other guard while being invisible to this register.
`checkout` is OURS: it is the door, not a vendor. The same distinction `_money` records one
entry down, and the route's own author reached it independently — services/platform/src/index.ts
notes it is mounted at `/v1/checkout` RATHER than under a segment named for a merchant of record.
⚠️ THE TELL THAT WOULD MAKE THIS WRONG: if the segment were ever `/paddle`, this entry would be
the wrong answer and a provider row would be the right one. The vendor behind the door is Paddle;
the door is ours. Naming the door after the vendor is what turns a resource into a tell.
_money: 🟢 `money` WAS ADDED BECAUSE THIS LIMB CAUGHT IT — the second time in two days, on a change that
had already passed every other guard. services/platform/src/routes/money.ts mounts
POST /v1/money/:provider ([pipeline 5]M-1, the merchant-of-record webhook) and CI went red naming
a segment nobody had classified. `money` is OURS: it is the door, not a vendor.
⚠️ AND THE PROVIDER IS A `:param`, WHICH THIS LIMB DROPS BY DESIGN. So adding Lemon Squeezy's
adapter tomorrow adds NO new literal segment, and the K-5 property this limb exists for — 'a new
payment webhook cannot land without somebody writing its name down' — would not fire here. That
is not a hole, and it is not left to a comment either: the provider set is DATA in
now FAILS when a registered rail has no row in THIS FILE. The obligation moved to the register
that actually knows the provider set, rather than being satisfied by a URL shape.
Paddle's row keeps `reachableAt: null` deliberately: the reverse check requires the last segment
of `reachableAt` to appear as a LITERAL route segment somewhere in services/**, and `paddle` never
does — it is resolved from the registry at request time. Claiming `/v1/money/paddle` would make
this file assert something no route registration says.
_account: 🟢 `account` WAS ADDED BECAUSE THIS LIMB CAUGHT IT, which is the whole point and worth recording.
services/platform/src/routes/account.ts (DELETE /v1/account, [pipeline B-5]) landed on main WHILE
this register was being written. The guard went red on the next run naming the new segment: a route
nobody had classified as ours or as a provider's. It is ours — the erasure route — so it is claimed
here rather than given a provider row. That is the limb working on a real, unplanned change on its
first day, rather than on a fixture.
_plan: 🟢 `plan` AND `cancel` WERE ADDED BECAUSE THIS LIMB CAUGHT THEM — the third time in three days,
on a change that had already passed every other guard. services/platform/src/routes/cancellation.ts
mounts POST /v1/plan/cancel ([pipeline 5]M-9, the ROSCA cancel path) and CI went red naming two
Both are OURS and neither is a vendor tell. `plan` is the thing the user bought, in the chassis's
own vocabulary — deliberately not "subscription", which [pipeline C-10] bans from shared code as
apps/subscriptiontracker's domain noun. `cancel` is the verb. No merchant of record is named in either, and none
can be: the route resolves the subscription from the verified session, never from the request.
nonProviderRouteSegments._appleToken: ⏱ 2026-09-16 · O-SIWA-TOKEN-NOT-REVOKED-ON-DELETE. `apple-token` is OURS, not a provider's tell: PUT /v1/account/apple-token is the app handing us the user's Apple refresh token so the account deletion can revoke it at Apple. Nothing calls IN on it — it is not a webhook, takes no provider signature, and is behind platformAuth like the rest of /v1/account. The call OUT to Apple is in services/platform/src/lib/provider-revoke.ts and reaches appleid.apple.com, never this Worker. ⏱ 2026-09-24 · `provider-token` is the same resource of ours for any provider (PUT /v1/account/provider-token, O-GOOGLE-SIGN-IN-NOT-BUILT): the app hands us the user's Apple or Google refresh token, and the call OUT to Google, from the same file, reaches oauth2.googleapis.com.
nonProviderRouteSegments._ext: ⏱ 2026-09-24 · O-EXTENSION-ACCOUNT-CHECK-UNBUILT. `ext`, `codes`, `token` and `revoke` are OURS, not a provider's tell: POST /v1/ext/codes (the signed-in nikatru.com/ext/connect page mints a one-time code), POST /v1/ext/token (the browser extension exchanges it, PKCE S256, for a per-device credential) and POST /v1/ext/revoke (that credential revokes itself) are the extension account check in services/platform/src/routes/ext.ts. None is a webhook and none takes a provider signature: the callers are our own page and our own extension. `token` is spelled like an OAuth endpoint because it is one — of ours. ⏱ 2026-09-30 · EXA-11: `devices` is ours too — GET /v1/ext/devices and DELETE /v1/ext/devices/:link_id are the ACCOUNT listing and revoking its own linked browsers, behind platformAuth; no provider calls them.
nonProviderRouteSegments._fx: ⏱ 2026-09-28 · ST-I3. `fx` and `latest` are OURS, not a provider's tell: GET /v1/fx/latest serves the ECB euro reference rates the nightly cron caches (services/platform/src/routes/fx.ts). It is a public READ of public data: nothing posts to it, it takes no body and no signature, and no user data goes in or out. The ECB is where the Worker READS the table from (services/platform/src/fx.ts); it receives nothing about anybody, so it is no processor and has no row among the providers.
nonProviderRouteSegments._native: ⏱ 2026-09-28 · ST-N1 (O-BOXA-CAPTCHA-REFUSES-NATIVE-SIGN-IN). `auth`, `native`, `signup` and `recover` are OURS, not a provider's tell: POST /v1/auth/native/<app>/{token,signup,recover,resend} (services/platform/src/routes/native-auth.ts) is a native app's captcha-free sign-in, sign-up, password-reset request and confirmation re-send, forwarded by the platform Worker to our own self-hosted GoTrue with the service-role bearer. The callers are our own native builds; nothing external posts here, and no provider signature is taken. The path segments are GoTrue's own endpoint names, because gotrue-dart builds exactly these from a base URL.

resend.why: ⏱ 2026-09-28 · ST-N1. POST /v1/auth/native/<app>/resend is GoTrue's own `/resend` endpoint (re-send a sign-up or email-change confirmation), called by our native builds and forwarded to our self-hosted GoTrue. It is NOT a Resend webhook: Resend never calls it and it takes no Resend signature. The one real link is the other way round — GoTrue sends that email through Resend, which is already this register's `resend` row (role email_delivery, disclosed); this route adds no new party.

_attest: ⏱ 2026-09-29 · ADR no.NNN (native sign-in serves only attested app installs). `attest`, `challenge` and `install` are RESOURCES OF OURS under
POST /v1/auth/native/:app/attest/{challenge,install}: a single-use challenge the native sign-in
attestation binds to, and an app install registering its signing key. Neither is a provider tell:
no payment or identity provider posts to them, and both are behind the fail-closed native limiters.
_handoff: ⏱ 2026-10-01 · O-DESKTOP-EMAIL-SIGN-IN-HAS-NO-ATTESTED-PATH. `handoff` and `code` are RESOURCES OF OURS under
POST /v1/auth/handoff/:app/code (the signed-in nikatru.com/app/connect page mints a desktop app's PKCE-bound
sign-in code) and POST /v1/auth/native/:app/handoff/token (the app exchanges it). Neither is a provider tell:
no payment or identity provider posts to them; the first is JWT-authenticated, the second sits behind the
fail-closed native edge limiter and refuses any browser.

roles._why: The vocabulary rows are validated against, declared once HERE rather than inside the guard — the same reason keyKinds lives in tooling/channel-register.json. Renaming a role out from under the rows still using it fails.
roles._sellerIsWhy: ⏱ 2026-09-26 · O-PRIVACY-OMITS-THE-INDIA-SELLER. `sellerIs` answers, per ROLE, who a buyer contracts with when a provider in that role takes the payment: `provider` (the provider itself sells: a store, a merchant of record), `nikatru` (Nikatru sells and the provider processes the payment on our behalf: a gateway), `never` (the provider must never be described as the seller) or `not-applicable` (the role takes no payment). It is a fact about the role, not about a channel, which is why it lives here and not in tooling/channel-register.json. assert-policy-claims reads it for every `seller-by-rail` row of tooling/legal/policy-claims.json: the rail resolves to its provider through `requiredWhen.rail` (tooling/legal/required-providers.mjs providersOnRail), and each listed page must state that provider's seller answer.

store_billing.means: an app store that sells to the user and pays us. It is the seller of record for that sale and we never see the card.

merchant_of_record.means: the legal seller for anything sold outside an app store. It collects and remits sales tax worldwide and is who the buyer contracted with.

payment_gateway.means: processes a card payment on our behalf. NOT the seller — we remain the seller, and the tax duty stays with us.

iap_aggregator.means: normalises store purchase events into one entitlement feed. Holds purchase state, not payment instruments.

infrastructure.means: runs or hosts the Services. Sees traffic and whatever the Services store, and is disclosed as a processor rather than as a seller.

identity.means: authenticates users and holds account credentials.

email_delivery.means: sends the transactional email the Services generate — sign-in links, verification. Holds the recipient address in order to deliver to it, and is disclosed as a processor. NOT a marketing channel: a mailing list is a separate purpose with its own consent (ConsentPurpose.marketingEmail) and would be its own disclosure.

content_delivery.means: serves a file the Services load into the visitor's browser at run time — a script, a font, a WebAssembly runtime. It sees that request (the visitor's IP address, user agent and referrer) and nothing the Services store. Disclosed as a party the browser contacts, not as a processor of stored data, and never a seller.

_why: ⏱ 2026-10-03 · rv2-business 024. The vocabulary rows are
validated against, declared once HERE for the reason `roles` is: until today `status` was free text,
and every guard that reads it (assert-policy-claims.mjs §3(c) and the egress limb, assert-purchase-path
.mjs I4) tested it against its own hard-coded set, so a misspelt status read as 'being pursued' in one
guard and 'not happening' in another. `silent` is the one property the guards share: a silent status
is a row for a thing we are NOT doing, so a missing disclosure is not a gap and does not print, and a
page or a route that reaches it anyway is a contradiction. Every other status is being pursued.

live.means: the provider is in use today: an account exists and the Services reach it.

wired-not-live.means: the code reaches the provider and the disclosure is drafted, but nothing is processed through it in production yet.

deferred.means: a decision we have not taken yet: the facts are recorded so the choice is not re-researched under time pressure, and nothing is pursued until it is taken.

retired.means: a decision we took and reversed: the provider was chosen or pursued once and is withdrawn by a dated record. The row stays so the retirement is visible and the facts are not rediscovered; nothing routes to it and nothing names it.

not-named-not-wired.means: no published page names the provider and no shipped code or policy reaches it; the row exists so that reaching it fails rather than passes silently.

_why: 🔴 THE SINK VOCABULARY. Declared HERE and not inside the guard, for the same reason `roles` above is:
renaming a category out from under the rows still using it must FAIL rather than quietly mean nothing.
WHY THIS EXISTS AT ALL, and it is worth stating in full because the defect it answers was PUBLISHED.
privacy.html said 'We do not collect or store your IP address'. The self-hosted GlitchTip on the Oracle
box was storing `user.ip_address`, re-observed on two independent events. NO GUARD COULD SEE IT:
· assert-policy-claims.mjs compares published TEXT to repo TEXT — it can prove the site says what
the repo says and nothing more, and both false statements passed it;
· the one claim row that IS typed `code` asserts `absent(cf-connecting-ip)` over ONE file, and its
own `why` concedes it 'is not a dataflow proof';
· tooling/legal/data-inventory.json declares 19 stores and EVERY ONE is Cloudflare D1 or KV. The
strings `glitchtip`, `oracle`, `sentry` and `ip_address` appear nowhere in it. The only
personal-data store outside Cloudflare was invisible BY CONSTRUCTION.
This register is the one artifact that already knew the crash rail is a live infrastructure sink of
its own — the row was `oracle-cloud` when this paragraph was written and is `hostinger` since the
2026-09-02 move. So the declaration is attached to the thing that knows the sink exists.
`tells` are how a category is recognised in a PUBLISHED DENIAL — the words a reader would see, not the
column names. They are matched against the text AFTER the denial verb, so 'We receive confirmation of
the purchase but do not collect or store your full card or bank details' is scoped to the object of
the denial and not to the whole sentence. A tell that is too narrow makes a future denial UNSCOPEABLE
(which FAILS); a tell that is too broad makes it INTERSECT (which FAILS). Neither direction passes
quietly, which is why erring is safe here and guessing is not.

ip_address.what: The network address a request came from, in a form that still identifies the connection. Personal data under GDPR and India's DPDP. ⚠️ GlitchTip's `scrub_ip_addresses` flag ANONYMISES (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /64) and then STORES — an anonymised prefix is still this category, which is exactly why the flag reading `True` hid the breach for weeks.

ip_fingerprint.what: A salted, one-way fingerprint of a network address, used as an abuse counter key and discarded within the hour. A DIFFERENT category from ip_address on purpose, and the published page draws the same line ('The fingerprint is not reversible to an IP address'). The construction is keyed (crypto.subtle.sign), not a digest — an unsalted sha256 of an IPv4 address is reversible by exhausting 2^32 values and would BE the address wearing a hash.

crash_report.what: An exception, its stack trace and the app/platform/version context around it. Received by GlitchTip, which we run ourselves.

usage_event.what: One record that a feature of an app was used, written only after consent.

install_identifier.what: The random per-install identifier (`anon_id`) that makes usage records pseudonymous rather than anonymous. Not a name, not an email, not an advertising ID — but stable, so records from one installation group together.
tells: random identifier created on your device

approximate_location.what: Country, region and city, derived at the network edge from an address that is then discarded. Coarse by construction; it is not a coordinate.

consent_record.what: The append-only record that a consent decision was made: which install, when, granted or withdrawn, and which policy version was shown.

email_address.what: A plain email address, as typed. Held by the launch-notification signup list, and present verbatim inside a merchant-of-record notification.

buyer_billing_details.what: The buyer's name and billing country, as they arrive inside a merchant-of-record notification stored VERBATIM ([pipeline 5]M-2 — a re-serialised or redacted copy can never be re-verified against the signature it came with).

entitlement_record.what: What a person has paid for: one row per (user, app, entitlement).

account_identifier.what: The account id a row is keyed on (a Supabase `sub`, or a store/aggregator user id). Not a credential.

user_content.what: What a person created inside an app — for apps/subscriptiontracker, the subscriptions they track and their budget figures. User-entered content about their own finances.
tells: what you created inside an app

payment_instrument.what: A card or bank number, CVV, IBAN or equivalent — the instrument itself. NOTHING in this factory receives this category, and no migration may declare a column for one (asserted separately by the `full card or bank details` claim row in policy-claims.json).

_why: 🔴 THE HALF THAT MAKES THE DENIAL LIMB UNFAKEABLE, and it is DATA rather than a list inside the guard
for exactly the reason `nonProviderRouteSegments` is. The guard extracts every "we do not collect /
do not store X" clause from the visible text of the published pages. A denial is allowed to exist
only if it resolves to a category in `dataCategories` above — or is written down HERE with a reason.
So publishing 'we do not store your precise location' turns the build RED until somebody either adds
the category (and therefore has to say whether a live sink receives it) or classifies the sentence as
not being about a data category at all. There is no third option, and no way to pad this list except
by naming the sentence you are adding.
⚠️ A row here is checked in BOTH directions: one whose denial no longer appears on its page FAILS, so
an exemption cannot outlive the sentence it was granted for — the same rule `disclosureGaps` carry
through `stillTrue`. And a row that DOES resolve to a category FAILS as inert: an exemption for
something that is not there reports judgement over nothing.

rows.denial: do not knowingly collect personal information from anyone under 18
rows.why: §8, the age requirement. This denies collecting anything at all FROM A CLASS OF PERSON (anyone under 18 - the single floor set by [ADR 068] on the DPDP Act 2023 threshold, replacing the earlier under-13 wording on 2026-09-05) — it is scoped by WHO, not by WHAT. Scoping it against a sink's category list would be a category error in the literal sense: every category would intersect it, and the guard would go red on a sentence that is true. The duty it belongs to is age-assurance, which is carried as a row in tooling/legal/duty-matrix.json where the trigger can be stated.

_why: Read by the EGRESS limb of tooling/ci/assert-policy-claims.mjs (2026-09-11), which takes every host a shipped Content-Security-Policy
(apps/*/web/_headers, sites/*/_headers) lets a browser reach and requires it to be ours or to carry a provider row's tell.
A host on one of these domains, or any subdomain of one, is ours. The vendor BEHIND it — Cloudflare for subscriptiontracker-api.nikatru.com, Hostinger
for glitchtip.nikatru.com — is already its own row and is disclosed as that vendor, not as a hostname.
Declared here, not inside the guard, for the reason `roles` is: a list inside a guard is a list nobody reviews with the register.
⏱ 2026-10-01 · SYN-P1's CLASS FIX (O-GOOGLE-WORKSPACE-AND-DRIVE-UNDISCLOSED). tooling/ops/register.json
